subject: Latency playbook, appointment & traffic artifacts
messages:
From: Paul Scott <pscott@streamline.health>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency playbook, appointment & traffic artifacts

Thanks for the time today — quick summary from Streamline's side and a few firm asks so we can get the probe scheduled. Appreciate Kim and Ben walking through Redwood's serving model. Key SLO targets we discussed that matter for our customer UX: p95 end-to-end <= 250 ms, p99 end-to-end <= 1.2 s for our primary "quick-replies" endpoint. For streaming endpoints (real-time assistant) we need per-chunk latency to be consistent and not have > 2s stalls during an active stream.

Traffic profile notes (high level):
- Sustained: ~140 QPS across our primary region (us-east)
- Burst: up to ~360 QPS for short windows (1–3 min) tied to product events
- Concurrency: 40–60 active streaming sessions at peak per service shard
- Typical request/response token envelope: request ~300–400 tokens, response ~600–900 tokens

Operational asks from Streamline:
1) We need a short playbook that maps Redwood test modes (shadow, canary, live probe) to what metrics you'll collect and the tolerated thresholds for p95/p99 during the probe.
2) A synthetic traffic envelope CSV we can use to run parallel load tests from our side (we shared an example during the call).
3) A proposed 2-hour window to run a live canary/probe with a small set of real traffic and synthetic amplification — target week of Jun 12 (we're flexible on day).
4) Clarify whether Redwood's prefix/KV cache and model-variant fallback are part of the hosted test or require a Dedicated config for parity.

If you can send a short playbook and test artifacts today, we can lock the date with Eng Ops. Also send any runbook artifacts we should expect to see in the probe report (percentile distributions, CPU/GPU utilization, kv-cache hit rates).

Paul
Paul Scott
Director, Platform Engineering
Streamline Health

Attachments: sample-request-traces.ndjson (attached by Streamline)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Scott <pscott@streamline.health>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency playbook, appointment & traffic artifacts

Thanks Paul — great meeting. See a concise playbook and the traffic artifact you can use attached. I’ve kept this intentionally prescriptive so Eng Ops can start wiring the tests without back-and-forth. High-level responses inline below, then next steps.

Inline answers to your asks: 
1) Playbook (attached: kim_playbook_v1.pdf) — maps Redwood modes: shadow (no cache priming, cold KV), canary (small % of traffic, full cache enabled), live probe (full feature set). For the canary we target p95 <= 250 ms and p99 <= 1.2 s. During the live probe we accept temporary p99 excursions up to 1.5 s provided we maintain no user-facing timeouts and we capture root-cause traces.
2) Traffic envelope (attached: traffic-envelope.csv) — includes target QPS timeline, concurrency ramps, and token-length distributions. Use this to drive your k6 script.
3) Proposed window — Jun 12–16 is good for Redwood. We recommend the following concrete window: Jun 14, 14:00–16:00 UTC for the 2-hour live probe (we'll reserve capacity). Please confirm.
4) Cache/fallback — hosted tests will enable prefix/KV cache and model-variant fallback by default. If you need identical hardware-level parity (same GPU families & kernel selection) we offer a Dedicated trial, but for SLO qualification hosted tests are representative for p95/p99 comparisons. We call out in the playbook when results may diverge because of hardware differences.

Operational/measurement details we will provide in the probe report:
- Per-request trace-id mapping to p95/p99 buckets
- Per-model and per-route token counts and throughput
- GPU utilization and queue lengths (90s granularity)
- KV-cache hit rates and warmup timeline
- Stream chunk timing distribution (per-chunk latency, stall counts)

Next steps (action items):
- Streamline: confirm Jun 14 14:00–16:00 UTC (reply-all). Please attach any IP allowlist or egress constraints for the probe.
- Streamline: upload a 30–60 minute representative trace sample (ndjson) if you want us to calibrate the synthetic generator to mirror real session behavior.
- Redwood: we'll share an ICS for the probe, a short k6 script template, and an expectation checklist by EOD.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: kim_playbook_v1.pdf, traffic-envelope.csv

Adding a couple of operational clarifications from the infra side so expectations align before the probe: 
- During the canary and live probe we'll capture both edge egress latency and server-side tail at the model host. For comparisons vs incumbent please note we report application-level end-to-end (ingress -> response written) so any CDN or proxy truncation should be accounted for on Streamline's side.
- Recommended probe config we suggest Redwood run for parity testing: 4 model-serving workers (1:1 with GPU), request batch size = 1 for streaming SLOs, and forced periodic KV-cache evictions during one of the ramp steps to exercise warm/cold behavior.
- If Streamline expects strict p99 < 1.2 s in all windows we will need to scope a Dedicated trial because multi-tenant hardware variance can produce higher tail variance for certain token envelopes; we will still run hosted probes and annotate the report.

Operational ask for Streamline: please share the IP ranges to allow for the k6 fetchers and the name of the internal Eng Ops on-call for the probe window. Also confirm whether you want us to perform TLS termination test vectors (mutual TLS vs standard TLS).

I'll draft the s3 bucket layout for results and share a short README in the drive link Kim posted.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
